flowers.text: If the proposed species IDs hold, yellow and white blooms would be expected from the tan and grey groups respectively. Keep flower photographs linked to the head that produced them; no flowering is recorded.

habitat.text: Lithops are southern African succulents adapted to living among stones in dry habitats. This planter combines two nursery appearance groups, provisionally L. lesliei and L. salicola. It recreates neither species' exact habitat, and a shared container does not show that their water needs or replacement stages will coincide.

lookalikes.name: Split rock
lookalikes.text: Pleiospilos nelii has rounder speckled leaves and a deeper cleft than the flatter windowed Lithops heads.

mature.text: A small cluster can form as some Lithops produce extra heads. The four visible heads currently came from two nursery pots; neither individual count nor root connections have been established.

nameStory.text: The name Lithops evokes a stone-like face: the disguise belongs to living leaves rather than a cactus stem.
